::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** 8th Aug. 1860.  
**From:** H. V.,  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown. Printed in <i>[Musings over the Christian Year](cmy_books/cmybook_88.qmd)</i>, xlvii.
:::

[To [FMY](people/person_1606.qmd) and CMY]

My dear Friends,

Forgive us for not having remembered to write to you yesterday. Our dear [Sister](people/person_796.qmd)[^1] departed like a babe from its mother’s arms with hardly a shudder, seemingly in the midst of a sweet sleep which had lasted a great many hours. God be thanked for her, and may He pour His rich blessings on you and all who love her.

It was at 9.30 yesterday morning; [my wife](people/person_795.qmd) was poorly, but both she and [my brothers wife](people/person_797.qmd) seem comfortably rested to-day.

In haste and love, yours always

[J. K.](people/person_798.qmd)

---

[^1]: Keble’s eldest sister, Elizabeth Keble (1789/90-7 August 1860).
